headline: Guardrails Before Growth
thesis: As EdTech Week opens at Columbia, the sector's message is that AI needs evidence, governance and teacher-led rollout before it scales.
summary: Governance and evidence dominate. EdSurge reports an EdReports finding that only one of 10 vendors offered third-party proof their AI features improve learning, and that nearly 30% of K-12 AI policies restrict or prohibit use. Inside Higher Ed surveys show faculty worry about critical thinking while students want clearer institutional direction, and EdTech Magazine and THE Journal both flag shadow AI as a data-privacy risk. Brookings advises targeted, well-designed AI over general-purpose tools. Events: EdTech Week NYC (Oct 14–15 per organizer), 1EdTech Technical Congress (Oct 19–21, Milwaukee) and ISTE+ASCD Boston (June 27–30, 2027).
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · October 14, 2026 · Direct site fetches were unavailable, so items come from search-indexed results; search-metadata dates can be inconsistent and EdTech Week dates vary by listing (Oct 12–16 vs. Oct 13–15 vs. Oct 14–15). Most sources had no new dated news today.
